text:
sasha: Heads-up, we're seeing pods in eu-west3-gpu-03 with a spike in TCP resets and gRPC errors since ~09:10 UTC. Apps report transient failures when contacting the model shards.

mohan: hmm, any kernel logs? could be conntrack.

sasha: grabbed node logs: 
```
Jun 18 09:12:14 node-eu-west3-gpu-03 kernel: [1234567.890] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Jun 18 09:12:14 node-eu-west3-gpu-03 kernel: [1234567.891] ip_conntrack: table full
```

yves: that looks like nf_conntrack exhaustion. Run `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` and `conntrack -L | wc -l` on the node.

sasha: ran them, results: `nf_conntrack_max=262144`, `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> `262144`. It's pegged.

anna-oncall: quick note: this started right after a burst of small inference jobs from dedicated GPU pool (autoscaler bounced workers up). Lots of short-lived outbound connections to internal shard endpoints.

mohan: pattern makes sense: many clients doing ephemeral connect->request->close without keepalives = large conntrack growth. Also kube-proxy iptables mode does SNAT for pod->pod across nodes which leaks entries.

sasha: oh, we also have the model runtime opening many short HTTP/1.1 connections (no pooling) from sidecars.

infra-bot: incident recorded: INC-2026-06-18-EW3-PORT-EXH (auto). Paging oncall.

mohan: mitigations (short term):
- increase nf_conntrack_max (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288`)
- drop conntrack state for TIME_WAIT-only flows faster (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=10`)
- enable connection pooling / persistent gRPC connections in runtime (app change)
- set `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` lower for bursty ephemeral patterns

yves: medium-term:
- move kube-proxy to IPVS (reduces SNAT churn) or switch to eBPF-based kube-proxy (Cilium) to avoid so many conntrack entries
- allocate a larger SNAT pool per node (cloud NAT config) or use node-local SNAT to spread mappings
- consider hostNetwork for inter-shard traffic where safe (bypasses kube NAT)

anna-oncall: is RDMA relevant here? some of these nodes have RDMA NICs for GPU interconnects.

mohan: RDMA traffic doesn't use conntrack/NAT if it's direct RoCE; the problem is TCP over IP between pods across nodes. RDMA unaffected unless app falls back to TCP.

sasha: immediate action taken: increased nf_conntrack_max to 524288 on the 6 most affected nodes and added a short sysctl tweak for TIME_WAIT. Also rolled a temporary routing change to prefer intra-node placement for shards to reduce east-west hops.

yves: nice. Can we throttle the autoscaler bursts? the scale-up pattern is the root cause. We should add a small ramp window to avoid thousands of short-living clients landing simultaneously.

mohan: +1. Also we should patch the model runtime to reuse HTTP/2 or gRPC streams and add keepalive backoffs. I'll open a PR for the runtime client.

anna-oncall: monitoring note: added alert for conntrack usage > 70% per node and a dashboard panel for ephemeral port exhaustion across GPU pools.

sasha: FYI logs also show a bunch of `SYN, RST` from kube-proxy timing out; I saved a pcap and put it in the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-06-18-ew3-port-exh/pcap/syn-rst.pcap`

yves: actions:
1) infra: roll sysctl increase cluster-wide for a couple hours and rollback if no regressions (mohan + sasha)
2) infra: evaluate ipvs/eBPF migration POC (yves)
3) runtime: patch client to pool connections (mohan)
4) autoscaler: add ramp window config to GPU pool (anna-oncall)

infra-bot: runbook step applied: increased conntrack limit on targeted nodes.

mohan: after sysctl bump, conntrack usage dropped (we forced kube-proxy reconcile) and pod errors dropped from 4.2% -> 0.3% in the affected pool. Still want the long-term changes.

sasha: leaving this thread open until we have PR + migration plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:
